আপনি প্রতিদিন যে website বা web app use করেন — Facebook, Daraz, bKash, Google Docs — সেগুলো release-এর আগে কেউ test করে। সেই কাজের নাম Web Application Testing। সহজ কথায়: browser-এ app খুলে দেখা — user-এর মতো ব্যবহার করে সব ঠিকমতো কাজ করছে কিনা।

এই post-এ শুধু theory নয় — real-world example, step-by-step scenario, এবং practical checklist দিয়ে বোঝানো হয়েছে। Junior QA, Developer, বা নতুন যারা Web Testing শিখতে চান — সবার জন্য সহজ high-level guide।

---

এক লাইনে — Web Application Testing কী?

Browser-এ web app open করে user-এর মতো test করা — feature কাজ করে কিনা, data ঠিক save হয় কিনা, error হলে message clear কিনা, payment/security ঠিক আছে কিনা।

দোকান Analogy — সবচেয়ে সহজ উদাহরণ:

নতুন দোকান খোলার আগে মালিক check করে — দোকানের signboard দেখা যায়? (UI) · দরজা খোলে? (App launch) · cash register কাজ করে? (Payment) · wrong price দিলে warning দেয়? (Validation) · চোর ঢুকতে পারে? (Security)। Web app testing = এই same idea, কিন্তু digital দোকানে।

---

Web App আর Website-এর পার্থক্য (জানা দরকার)

বিষয় Static Website Web Application
ExampleCompany portfolio, blogDaraz, Gmail, bKash, ERP system
User actionশুধু read/browseLogin, form fill, payment, data save
BackendMinimal বা নেইAPI + Database + Authentication
Testing focusLayout, links, contentFunctionality, security, data, flow

আমরা এই post-এ Web Application testing নিয়ে কথা বলছি — যেখানে user login করে, data submit করে, transaction করে।

---

Web App-এর ভেতরে কী কী থাকে?

User শুধু browser দেখে, কিন্তু ভেতরে ৩টা layer কাজ করে:

১. Frontend (যা user দেখে)

Button, form, menu, color, mobile view — Chrome DevTools দিয়ে inspect করা যায়।

২. Backend API (যা user দেখে না)

Server-এ request যায়, business logic চলে, response আসে। UI-তে "Order placed" দেখালেও API fail হতে পারে — তাই দুটোই check করতে হয়।

৩. Database (data store)

User register করলে database-এ save হয়। UI-তে success দেখালেও DB-তে data না গেলে bug।

Real Example — E-commerce Order:

User "Place Order" click করে → Frontend request পাঠায় → API stock check + price calculate করে → Database-এ order save → Payment gateway call → Success page show। Test করতে হবে: UI message, API response (200/400), DB-তে order record, payment status — চারটা layer।

---

কেন Web Application Testing দরকার?

Production-এ bug গেলে real damage হয়:

  • Payment bug — customer double charge, company reputation নষ্ট
  • Login bug — user account-এ ঢুকতে পারে না, support call বাড়ে
  • Data bug — wrong report, wrong salary, legal issue
  • Security bug — hacker অন্য user-এর data দেখে, fine + lawsuit

Real-world bug story (common):

E-commerce site-এ coupon code apply করলে UI-তে ৳500 discount দেখায়, কিন্তু payment gateway-এ full amount cut হয়। Customer complain → refund → brand trust loss। Root cause: Frontend calculation ঠিক, API/payment integration test হয়নি।

---

Testing Types — সহজ ভাষায় + Real Example

১. Functional Testing — "Feature কাজ করে?"

App-এর প্রতিটি feature expected মতো কাজ করছে কিনা check করা।

Example — Food Delivery App:

  • Restaurant list load হয়?
  • Cart-এ item add/remove?
  • Delivery address save?
  • Order track page update হয়?

২. UI/UX Testing — "User বUnderstand করতে পারে?"

Button click করা যায়? Error message readable? Mobile-এ text cut হয় না?

Example: Login fail হলে "Invalid credentials" দেখায় — "Error 500" না। Submit button disabled থাকা উচিত empty form-এ।

৩. Compatibility Testing — "সব browser/device-এ চলে?"

Chrome-এ OK মানে Safari/mobile-এ OK নয় — আলাদা test দরকার।

Example: Admin dashboard Chrome desktop-এ perfect, কিন্তু iPhone Safari-এ sidebar overlap — compatibility bug।

৪. Performance Testing — "অনেক user একসাথে থাকলে?"

1000 user Black Friday sale-এ login দিলে site slow/crash হয়?

৫. Security Testing — "অনুমতি ছাড়া access?"

Normal user admin panel দেখতে পারে? SQL injection কাজ করে?

Example: URL-এ /orders/1001 change করে /orders/1002 দিলে অন্য customer-এর order দেখা যায় — critical security bug।

৬. Regression Testing — "নতুন fix পুরনো কিছু ভাঙেছে?"

Login bug fix-এর পর cart feature break হয়েছে কিনা re-check।

---

Real-World Scenario — E-commerce (ShopBD) Full Test Day

ধরুন আপনি QA — আগামীকাল ShopBD e-commerce site release। আজ কী test করবেন?

Step 1: Smoke Test (১৫ মিনিট) — "App চালু যোগ্য?"

  1. Homepage open — crash না
  2. Login valid user — success
  3. Product page open — image load
  4. Cart page open — empty cart message

Smoke fail = dev team-কে বলুন, deep test শুরু করবেন না।

Step 2: Critical Flow Test (১–২ ঘণ্টা) — "Business money flow"

Register → Login → Search "phone" → Add to cart → Apply coupon
→ Checkout → bKash pay → Order confirmation → Email/SMS received

প্রতিটি step-এ positive (valid data) + negative (wrong coupon, insufficient stock) test করুন।

Step 3: Negative Testing Examples

আপনি কী করবেন Expected Result
Wrong password loginError message, account lock না (first attempt)
Empty cart checkout"Cart is empty" — payment page না
Expired coupon apply"Coupon expired" message
Payment cancel mid-wayOrder status PENDING, double charge না
Logout → Back buttonLogin page, protected page access না

Step 4: Cross-browser Quick Check

Critical flow একবার Chrome + একবার mobile view (DevTools responsive mode)।

Step 5: Bug Report (Jira-তে)

Title: Payment success but order status shows FAILED
Steps: 1. Login 2. Add product 3. Pay bKash 4. Return to site
Expected: Order status PAID
Actual: Order FAILED, money deducted
Environment: staging.shopbd.com, Chrome 120, Android 14
Screenshot: attached
---

Real-World Scenario — Banking / bKash Style App

Financial app-এ testing আরও careful — amount, OTP, session সব critical।

Must-test areas:

  • Login + OTP — wrong OTP 3 bar = lock?
  • Send money — wrong number, insufficient balance, own number
  • Amount field — 0, negative, 999999999, decimal
  • Session timeout — 5 min idle → auto logout?
  • Transaction history — send-এর পর history-তে correct entry?

Real bug pattern:

User ৳100 send করে, success screen দেখায়, কিন্তু receiver পায় ৳1000 — decimal/format bug। Test: 1, 10, 100, 100.50, 99999 — boundary values always test করুন।

---

Real-World Scenario — Admin Panel / ERP

Internal web app — employee, HR, inventory manage করে।

Typical test cases:

  • Admin user employee add/edit/delete (CRUD)
  • Normal employee admin menu দেখতে পারে না (role-based access)
  • Search filter: date range, department, status
  • Report download PDF/Excel — data accurate?
  • Pagination — page 2-এ duplicate record না

Example: HR "Delete Employee" click → confirmation popup → Yes → employee list-এ remove + login block। Delete ছাড়া direct URL hit করলে 403 Forbidden।

---

Manual vs Automation — কখন কী করবেন?

Situation Manual Automation
নতুন feature প্রথম bar✅ Explore, feel, edge case খুঁজুন❌
প্রতি sprint same login test❌ boring, slow✅ Automate
Release-এর আগে regressionCritical new area✅ Full suite run
UI color/spacing check✅ Human eyePartial (visual tools)

Beginner tip: শুরুতে manual দিয়ে flow বুঝুন → পরে critical path automate (Playwright/Cypress)।

---

Beginner-এর Practical Checklist — প্রথম দিন থেকে

নতুন project-এ QA assign হলে এই order follow করুন:

  1. App tour — ৩০ মিনিট user হিসেবে browse, note করুন main features
  2. Critical flows লিখুন — top 3 journey (login, main action, logout)
  3. Test account নিন — admin + normal user credentials
  4. Environment confirm — staging URL, test data, bug tool (Jira)
  5. Smoke run — app alive?
  6. Happy path — main flow end-to-end
  7. Negative cases — wrong input, empty field, unauthorized
  8. Bug report — clear steps + screenshot

Quick checklist table — যেকোনো web form

Test কী করবেন
Empty submitRequired field blank → error message?
Invalid formatemail: "abc" → validation?
Max length500 character name → truncate/error?
Special charsName: O'Brien,
content.en:
Every day you use web apps — Facebook, Amazon, online banking, Google Docs. Before release, someone tested them. That work is called Web Application Testing. In simple terms: open the app in a browser and use it like a real user to check that everything works correctly.

This post is not just theory. It uses real-world examples, step-by-step scenarios, and a practical checklist so beginners can understand easily. Whether you are a junior QA, developer, or completely new — this is your high-level guide.

---

In One Line — What Is Web Application Testing?

Open a web app in the browser and test it like a user — do features work, is data saved correctly, are error messages clear, are payment and security OK?

Shop Analogy — easiest way to understand:

Before opening a new shop, the owner checks — is the signboard visible? (UI) · does the door open? (App launch) · does the cash register work? (Payment) · does it warn on wrong price? (Validation) · can strangers enter the back office? (Security). Web app testing = same idea, but for a digital shop.

---

Web App vs Website — Know the Difference

Topic Static Website Web Application
ExampleCompany portfolio, blogAmazon, Gmail, banking portal, ERP
User actionRead and browse onlyLogin, submit forms, pay, save data
BackendMinimal or noneAPI + Database + Authentication
Testing focusLayout, links, contentFunctionality, security, data, flows

In this post we focus on Web Application testing — where users log in, submit data, and complete transactions.

---

What Is Inside a Web App?

Users only see the browser, but three layers work together:

1. Frontend (what the user sees)

Buttons, forms, menus, colors, mobile layout — inspectable with Chrome DevTools.

2. Backend API (what the user does not see)

Requests go to the server, business logic runs, response comes back. The UI may show "Order placed" even if the API failed — so you must check both.

3. Database (where data is stored)

When a user registers, data is saved in the database. The UI may show success even if nothing was saved — that is a bug.

Real Example — E-commerce Order:

User clicks "Place Order" → Frontend sends request → API checks stock and calculates price → Database saves order → Payment gateway is called → Success page shows. You must test: UI message, API response (200/400), DB record, payment status — all four layers.

---

Why Is Web Application Testing Important?

Bugs in production cause real damage:

  • Payment bug — double charge, lost customer trust
  • Login bug — users locked out, support calls spike
  • Data bug — wrong reports, wrong payroll, legal issues
  • Security bug — hackers see other users' data, fines and lawsuits

Real-world bug story (very common):

An e-commerce site shows a $50 discount in the UI after applying a coupon, but the payment gateway charges the full amount. Customer complains → refund → brand trust lost. Root cause: frontend calculation was correct, but API/payment integration was never tested.

---

Testing Types — Plain Language + Real Examples

1. Functional Testing — "Does the feature work?"

Check that each feature behaves as expected.

Example — Food Delivery App:

  • Does the restaurant list load?
  • Can you add/remove items from cart?
  • Does delivery address save?
  • Does the order tracking page update?

2. UI/UX Testing — "Can the user understand it?"

Are buttons clickable? Are error messages readable? Does text get cut off on mobile?

Example: On login failure, show "Invalid credentials" — not "Error 500". Submit button should stay disabled on an empty form.

3. Compatibility Testing — "Does it work everywhere?"

Works in Chrome does not mean works in Safari/mobile — test separately.

Example: Admin dashboard looks perfect on Chrome desktop, but sidebar overlaps on iPhone Safari — compatibility bug.

4. Performance Testing — "What if many users come at once?"

During a Black Friday sale, does the site become slow or crash when 1000 users log in?

5. Security Testing — "Can someone access without permission?"

Can a normal user open the admin panel? Does SQL injection work?

Example: Change URL from /orders/1001 to /orders/1002 and see another customer's order — critical security bug.

6. Regression Testing — "Did the new fix break something old?"

After fixing login, re-check that cart still works.

---

Real-World Scenario — E-commerce (ShopBD) Full Test Day

Imagine you are QA — ShopBD e-commerce releases tomorrow. What do you test today?

Step 1: Smoke Test (15 minutes) — "Is the app alive?"

  1. Open homepage — no crash
  2. Login with valid user — success
  3. Open product page — images load
  4. Open cart — empty cart message shows

If smoke fails, tell the dev team — do not start deep testing.

Step 2: Critical Flow Test (1–2 hours) — "Business money flow"

Register → Login → Search "phone" → Add to cart → Apply coupon
→ Checkout → Pay → Order confirmation → Email/SMS received

At each step, test positive (valid data) and negative (wrong coupon, out of stock).

Step 3: Negative Testing Examples

What You Do Expected Result
Login with wrong passwordError message, no lock on first attempt
Checkout with empty cart"Cart is empty" — no payment page
Apply expired coupon"Coupon expired" message
Cancel payment mid-wayOrder status PENDING, no double charge
Logout → press BackLogin page, no protected access

Step 4: Cross-browser Quick Check

Run critical flow once in Chrome and once in mobile view (DevTools responsive mode).

Step 5: Bug Report (in Jira)

Title: Payment success but order status shows FAILED
Steps: 1. Login 2. Add product 3. Pay 4. Return to site
Expected: Order status PAID
Actual: Order FAILED, money deducted
Environment: staging.shopbd.com, Chrome 120, Android 14
Screenshot: attached
---

Real-World Scenario — Banking / Wallet App

Financial apps need extra care — amount, OTP, and session are all critical.

Must-test areas:

  • Login + OTP — wrong OTP 3 times = account lock?
  • Send money — wrong number, insufficient balance, own number
  • Amount field — 0, negative, 999999999, decimal values
  • Session timeout — 5 min idle → auto logout?
  • Transaction history — after send, correct entry in history?

Real bug pattern:

User sends $100, success screen shows, but receiver gets $1000 — decimal/format bug. Test: 1, 10, 100, 100.50, 99999 — always test boundary values.

---

Real-World Scenario — Admin Panel / ERP

Internal web apps used by employees for HR, inventory, and management.

Typical test cases:

  • Admin adds/edits/deletes employee (CRUD)
  • Normal employee cannot see admin menu (role-based access)
  • Search filters: date range, department, status
  • Report download PDF/Excel — is data accurate?
  • Pagination — no duplicate records on page 2

Example: HR clicks "Delete Employee" → confirmation popup → Yes → removed from list + login blocked. Direct URL without delete flow should return 403 Forbidden.

---

Manual vs Automation — When to Use What?

Situation Manual Automation
New feature first time✅ Explore, feel, find edge cases❌
Same login test every sprint❌ boring, slow✅ Automate
Regression before releaseCritical new areas✅ Run full suite
UI color/spacing check✅ Human eyePartial (visual tools)

Beginner tip: Start manual to understand flows → then automate critical paths (Playwright/Cypress).

---

Practical Checklist for Beginners — From Day One

When assigned to a new project as QA, follow this order:

  1. App tour — browse as user for 30 minutes, note main features
  2. Write critical flows — top 3 journeys (login, main action, logout)
  3. Get test accounts — admin + normal user credentials
  4. Confirm environment — staging URL, test data, bug tool (Jira)
  5. Run smoke — is the app alive?
  6. Happy path — main flow end-to-end
  7. Negative cases — wrong input, empty fields, unauthorized access
  8. Report bugs — clear steps + screenshot

Quick checklist — any web form

Test What to Do
Empty submitLeave required field blank → error message?
Invalid formatemail: "abc" → validation?
Max length500 character name → truncate/error?
Special charsName: O'Brien, script tags → safe handling?
Double submitClick Pay twice → no duplicate charge
---

Tools — What Do You Need to Start?

You do not need many tools — these 4 cover 80% of work:

  • Browser (Chrome) — F12 DevTools: Network tab (see APIs), Console (errors), Mobile view
  • Postman — test APIs directly, verify login tokens
  • Screenshot tool — attach to bug reports
  • Jira / Excel — track test cases and bugs

Add later: Playwright (automation), JMeter (load testing).

DevTools Pro Tip:

Keep Network tab open when submitting forms. If UI shows "Success" but API returns 500 — the bug is in the backend. Screenshot status code + response body.

---

Common Mistakes — What New QA Engineers Do

  • Only happy path — test once with valid data and stop
  • Vague bug reports — "payment does not work" → dev cannot reproduce
  • Testing on production — changing real customer data — use staging
  • Ignoring APIs — UI looks fine but data is wrong
  • Same browser only — Chrome only, no mobile check
  • Critical flow last — testing payment on release day — disaster
---

Web Testing Flow in Agile (Real Sprint)

Monday: Dev deploys new build → QA smoke (20 min) → Pass → feature testing starts

Tuesday–Thursday: Test new stories + verify bugs + re-test fixes

Friday AM: Regression on critical flows (2–4 hours)

Friday PM: Release → Production smoke (10 min)

---

Related Topics — Go Deeper

  • Test Case Writing — step-by-step test documents
  • Smoke vs Sanity Testing — types of quick checks
  • Login API Test Cases — auth module in detail
  • Regression Testing — release confidence
  • Exploratory Testing — finding bugs without a script
---

Conclusion — Remember These 5 Things

  1. Think like a user — not like a developer
  2. UI + API + Data — verify all three layers together
  3. Critical flow first — login, payment, core business logic
  4. Test negative cases — wrong input, unauthorized access, edge cases
  5. Write clear bug reports — steps, expected, actual, screenshot

Learning Web Application Testing = practice. Pick a staging app, follow this checklist — your confidence will grow within a week.
